ritual: {name} poured milk upon the hearth-stones, and the smoke climbed straight to the sky-father.
{name} sang the old words to the fire. The fire answered with a crackle.
{name} set a bowl of grain beside the hearth for those who came before.
{name} named the cattle one by one, so the gods would know them.
ritualAtMound: {name} sat at the mound of {ancestor} until the shadows grew long, speaking of the herds.
{name} poured mead into the earth of {ancestor}'s mound. The grass seemed greener there.
{name} told {ancestor} the news of the camp. The wind carried the answer away.
burial: They raised the earth over {deceased}. {name} placed ochre on the body, red as the first dawn.
{deceased} was laid in the mound facing the sunrise, with a pot of food for the long road.
{name} spoke the name of {deceased} three times, and the band answered three times, and the mound was closed.

death.starvation: {deceased} grew thin as winter grass, and died hungry.
death.exposure: The cold took {deceased} in the night.
death.oldAge: {deceased} closed their eyes, old and full of days, and went down the road of the ancestors.

seasonTurn.spring: The ice broke on the river. The cows bellowed for new grass.
seasonTurn.summer: The sun stood high and long over the steppe.
seasonTurn.autumn: The geese flew south. The elders said: fill the pits.
seasonTurn.winter: Snow came on the north wind. The hearth is the whole world now.
